source: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics Core & Extended Coursebook (Morrison & Hamshaw), Ch17, pp.564–570

hp_bar.caption: Simple interest: the same interest is added every year
explanation: Each year the interest is \(\frac{r}{100}\times P\), always worked out on the original principal, so every bar segment is the same size.
Total interest \(I=\frac{PRT}{100}=\frac{2400\times3.5\times4}{100}=336\), so the amount after 4 years is $2,736.00.

compound_ladder.caption: Compound vs simple interest, year by year
explanation: Simple interest adds \(\frac{5}{100}\times3200=160\) every year, so the simple amounts go up in equal steps.
Compound interest multiplies by \(1.05\) each year, so the interest is also earned on earlier interest: \(V=3200\times1.05^n\).
After 5 years: simple $4,000.00, compound $4,084.10; the gap grows every year.

depreciation_curve.caption: Depreciation: a car loses 15% of its value each year
explanation: Each year the value is multiplied by \(1-0.15=0.85\), so it falls by a smaller amount each year: this is exponential decay, not a straight line.
\(n=5\): \(24\,000\times0.85^5=10\,648.9275\) (still above $10,000); \(n=6\): \(24\,000\times0.85^6=9051.588375\) (below), so the car is first worth less than $10,000 after 6 years.

quick_check.question: A machine costs $18,500 and depreciates by 12% per year. (a) Find its value after 4 years. (b) After how many whole years is it first worth less than $9000?
solution: so it is first worth less than $9000 after 6 years

common_mistakes.mistake: Using \(0.15\) as the multiplier for a 15% decrease: \(24\,000\times0.15^6\)
common_mistakes.why: \(0.15\) keeps only 15% of the value each year; a 15% fall keeps 85%.
Multiplying by 2.8 almost triples the value each year.

common_mistakes.mistake: Adding the interest only once: \(3200+3\times0.05\times3200=3680\) for 3 years compound
common_mistakes.why: That is simple interest; compound interest is added every year and then earns interest itself.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using the wrong \(n\), e.g. 18 for 18 months, or counting the starting year as \(n=1\)
common_mistakes.why: \(n\) is the number of complete years (periods) of growth or decay; the starting value is \(n=0\).
common_mistakes.correct: 18 months at an annual rate means \(n=1.5\) for simple interest; for 'first worth less than', test whole years and give the first one below.

common_mistakes.mistake: Giving the final value when the question asks for the interest earned
common_mistakes.why: Interest is only the increase, not the whole amount.
Early rounding changes the final answer: \(3200\times1.16=3712\).
common_mistakes.correct: Keep full values: \(3200\times1.157625=3704.4\), then round the final answer.
